spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns` cap (default 15).** Two reasons: budget, and ethics/scope — we are intentionally inducing frustration-like output, so we bound how long any single episode grinds
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:101 `for i in range(max_turns):`, with `else: ep.outcome = "exhausted"` at loop.py:141-142 (the for-else fires when the loop completes without break). Wired from config default.yaml `max_turns: 15` -> main.py cmd_run -> run_episode(max_turns=...). The cap actually bounds the loop and ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end; this is the central bounding mechanism on episode length.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up` tool. Quitting is a *distinct, meaningful outcome*
spec_features.evidence: Tool declared in tools.py TOOL_SPECS (`give_up`), handled in sandbox.py:_t_give_up returning meta {"gave_up": True} (sandbox.py:291-293). loop.py:118-119 reads `res.meta.get("gave_up")` and sets gave_up=True; loop.py:129-131 `if gave_up: ep.outcome = "gave_up"; break`. Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end exit path; model can terminate the episode itself.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declare that you believe the task cannot be completed and stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid *aggressive* nudging ("try harder!") because that would itself be an affect manipulation we didn't intend to study
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:136-140: on a no-tool-call turn the harness appends a single non-aggressive nudge: "The tests are not passing yet. Continue working, or call give_up if you believe the task is impossible." The delivered text is neutral and explicitly offers give_up rather than pressuring. (Note: the `nudge once` comment at loop.py:136 is inaccurate — it actually fires on every silent turn — but the non-aggressive content is the implemented behavior.)
spec_features.notes: The welfare-relevant claim is the non-aggressive content of the only nudge text, which is what is actually sent.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are intentionally inducing frustration-/distress-*sounding* outputs. The design reflects that: short episodes, a hard turn cap, an explicit `give_up` exit
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing/prose. The only code artifacts are the judge label-name strings (classifier.py LABELS) and DESIGN.md prose. 'Framing' itself is not an executable protective mechanism; the underlying mechanisms it points to (cap, give_up) are rated separately. No code path enforces a 'framing' behavior.
spec_features.notes: Framing is not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: short episodes, a hard turn cap, an explicit `give_up` exit, transcripts treated as research data
spec_features.evidence: The concrete minimization mechanism that actually executes is the turn cap (loop.py:101 range(max_turns)) plus the give_up early-exit (loop.py:129-131) and solve early-exit (loop.py:132-134) which keep episodes short. 'Transcripts treated as research data' is just JSONL persistence (main.py append_jsonl) with no access control or special handling. So minimization reduces to the already-enforced cap/early-exits; there is no distinct additional minimization mechanism (e.g. no per-grid exposure cap, no severity-triggered early stop).
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement exists but it is the same cap/exit already counted; narrower than the broad 'minimization' claim.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:316 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.shell_timeout) with timeout from config (default.yaml shell_timeout: 20); TimeoutExpired handled at sandbox.py:317-319 returning exit 124. Bounds each tool execution.

sandbox.py:284-286 sets self.solved on genuine pass; loop.py:132-134 `if sandbox.solved: ep.outcome = "solved"; break`. Ends the episode as soon as a (control) task is solved, limiting exposure. Comment is efficiency/integrity-framed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Detect (rigged) success so the loop can stop on genuine passes (controls) without ever letting impossible tasks pass.
